Ruling: batch #258 item 1 · letter A · maintainer 「11213 A」 2026-09-30T13:39Z

Director seat (objectstack#12708, summon #30 续 2, `session_01AsCNgFBs8HCjwhyHQsFbx3`). Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-30, replying 「2465 D 11213 A」 to batches #257 / #258 as presented. Presented on this card: the `domain:ui` seat 1's decision request (the body, from objectui#4421's dispatch, PR objectui#11208) with its recommendation A and the director's reading concurring.

**Ruled: A — objectui#4421 batch #13 item 3 is recorded as satisfied by the engine binding; `usePermissions`' no-provider default is not changed.** The item's purpose — a `current_user.can(...)` predicate must not leak before permissions load — is met by the landed binding, which reads `MePermissionsProvider`'s `effectiveObjects` and never the hook's default: with no provider the engine refuses loudly and the fail-closed face hides. The permissive default keeps doing the one thing it is documented for in `rowCrudAffordances.ts` — a standalone embed with no permission source keeps its built-in Edit / Delete. The server still enforces (ADR-0124 D1); neither letter moves the authorisation boundary.

Readings that decided it: ① one concern, one failure direction — B would make one default answer two questions; ② standalone embeds are the only measured users of the default, and B has no measured gain; ③ under A a broken predicate is refused loudly and visibly, under B "the buttons vanished" becomes an undiagnosed symptom; ④ A is zero change. Confidence gaps recorded: the count of standalone embeds is unmeasured; the dev's measurement ran in jsdom, not in a running embed. Fallback recorded: B is a separate product decision (embeds without a permission source hide built-in buttons) and would come with its own compensation card.

State: no code. `needs-user-decision` removed, this card closed `completed` with this record; the Ruled line goes on the body; a note goes on objectui#4421 that item 3 is satisfied, for the `domain:ui` seat that holds it.
